_comment: PLACEHOLDER VALUES - do not create this as-is.
A short Fargate service sample, assuming a cluster, a VPC with subnets, a security group, and an
ALB target group all already exist. Creating those is a networking decision with an owner, and a
sample that guessed at them would be a sample you have to undo.
Subsequent deploys are update-service, not create-service:
_comment_task_definition: Family name with no revision, which resolves to the latest ACTIVE revision at create time. Pin a
revision (saas-investigator:7) if you want the service to hold still while you register new ones.
_comment_desired_count: One task, and this is a constraint rather than a starting number.
A run's live step-by-step view lives in memory in the task that started the run - nothing about
it is written to MongoDB. So the request that subscribes to run events has to reach the same task
that accepted the POST which started it. With two tasks behind an ALB doing round-robin, roughly
half of those subscriptions hit a task that has never heard of that runId and get a 404, which
users experience as the live view intermittently not working.
Scaling past one needs stickiness on the ALB target group, which is not set here because it is a
property of the target group rather than of the service:
Everything else in the app is stateless: the JWT is signed rather than stored, and its signing
secret is resolved from the database so every task agrees on it.
See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, "The report is durable; the narration is not."
_comment_network: PLACEHOLDER subnet and security group IDs. awsvpc mode gives the task its own ENI.
assignPublicIp is ENABLED here only because a task in a public subnet with no NAT gateway needs a
public IP to reach anything outbound at all - and this app is entirely outbound-dependent: it
pulls its own image, crawls third-party sites, and calls a model API. Private subnets plus a NAT
gateway is the better shape; set this to DISABLED if that is what you have, and confirm the route
before you do, because the symptom of getting it wrong is a task that starts, passes its health
check, and fails every single run with a connection timeout.
The security group needs no inbound rule except from the load balancer's security group on 8080.
Outbound needs 443 to the model API and to whatever your sources are, plus MongoDB's port.
_comment_load_balancer: PLACEHOLDER target group ARN. containerName and containerPort must match the task definition
exactly ("app", 8080) or the service will not register any targets and will say very little
Configure the target group itself for two things this JSON cannot express:
1. A health check path of /actuator/health (unauthenticated by design). This is the check that
decides whether traffic reaches the task; the container health check in task-definition.json
decides whether ECS replaces it. Both, doing different jobs.
2. An idle timeout long enough for Server-Sent Events. Run progress and streamed answers are SSE,
and spring.mvc.async.request-timeout is 10 minutes because a NUCLEAR-depth run can take that
long. The ALB's default idle timeout is 60 seconds, which cuts the live execution view off
mid-run with no error the app can report - it is the connection, not the run, that died. Raise
it on the load balancer (not the target group): idle_timeout.timeout_seconds=600.
_comment_grace_period: 180s of load-balancer health checks ignored after a task starts. It has to comfortably exceed JVM
boot plus Mongo index verification and the admin-seed check, or the ALB marks the task unhealthy
while it is still starting, ECS replaces it, and the replacement does exactly the same thing - a
loop that looks like a broken application and is a misconfigured timeout.
_comment_deployment: With desiredCount 1, maximumPercent 200 means the new task starts before the old one stops, so
there is no gap in availability - at the cost of both serving traffic briefly, during which a
live view opened against one task while the run started on the other gets the 404 described
above. Set maximumPercent to 100 and minimumHealthyPercent to 0 if you would rather have a few
seconds of downtime per deploy than that overlap.
Circuit breaker on with rollback: a task that cannot start - a bad image tag, an execution role
that cannot read the secrets - rolls back to the last working definition instead of retrying
